findings.statement: CA9 is up in tumour at RNA (log2FC 6.312, padj 1.72e-49) and protein (log2FC 2.269, padj 9.9e-43), replicates in TCGA-KIRC (log2FC 9.712) and persists at purity 1 (RNA log2FC 7.787), so it is tumour-cell intrinsic. Girentuximab reached PHASE_3. CNV loss frequency is 0.145 and the cis rho is 0.224.

CD70 is up at RNA (log2FC 4.464, padj 4.13e-35) and protein (log2FC 2.421, padj 1.94e-38), replicates in TCGA-KIRC (log2FC 7.09) and keeps RNA log2FC 4.278 at purity 1. It is a membrane antigen with clinical-stage antibody candidates (cusatuzumab PHASE_2).

NNMT is up at RNA (log2FC 4.67, padj 2.04e-40) and protein (log2FC 2.709, padj 1.23e-43), replicates in TCGA-KIRC (log2FC 4.685) and is prognostic (Cox log HR 0.301, padj 0.00479, higher expression is worse). It ranks 4th in the target profile and 6th in the biomarker profile.

ENPP3 is up at RNA (log2FC 3.895), protein (log2FC 1.544, padj 3.02e-37) and TCGA-KIRC (log2FC 5.557), with RNA log2FC 5.278 at purity 1. It is a surface enzyme with an antibody-drug conjugate in PHASE_2 (AGS-16C3F). CNV loss frequency is 0.182.

SCARB1 is the top-ranked target (score 4.1314). It is up at RNA (log2FC 2.974, padj 7.23e-39) and protein (log2FC 1.837, padj 5.08e-37), replicates in TCGA-KIRC (log2FC 3.989) and holds at purity 1 (RNA log2FC 3.762). It is not prognostic (Cox log HR -0.038, padj 0.684).

SLC16A3 (MCT4) is up at RNA (log2FC 3.435) and protein (log2FC 2.279), replicates in TCGA-KIRC (log2FC 3.291) and has RNA log2FC 3.821 at purity 1. The cis rho is 0.258 and the DepMap ccRCC mean effect is -0.015, so it is not a selective dependency.

PSAT1 is the top biomarker (score 5.3696). It is down at RNA (log2FC -3.867, padj 2.54e-29) and protein (log2FC -1.963, padj 1.77e-33), replicates in TCGA-KIRC (log2FC -2.974), and higher expression predicts worse survival (Cox log HR 0.43, padj 5.66e-7). Its direction is opposite to the usual serine-pathway upregulation.

PCK1 is down at RNA (log2FC -4.424) and protein (log2FC -1.859), consistent with loss of proximal tubule gluconeogenic identity. TCGA-KIRC replicates the loss (log2FC -3.079), and low expression is prognostic (Cox log HR -0.415, padj 1.91e-7, higher expression protective).

ALDH6A1 is down at RNA (log2FC -3.399) and protein (log2FC -1.925). Its 14q loss frequency is 0.355 with a positive cis rho of 0.525, so copy loss contributes to the decrease. Higher expression is protective in TCGA-KIRC (Cox log HR -0.554, padj 9.45e-12).

FABP6 is up at RNA (log2FC 4.006) and protein (log2FC 1.921) and replicates in TCGA-KIRC (log2FC 6.431). The 5q gain frequency is 0.573 with a cis rho of 0.309, so the gain drives the increase. It is a tissue biomarker rather than a dependency (DepMap selectivity 0.033).

HK2 is up at RNA (log2FC 3.351) and protein (log2FC 2.106) and replicates in TCGA-KIRC (log2FC 3.974). It marks the glycolytic Warburg shift but shows no selective DepMap dependency (mean effect -0.123).

CA4 is down at RNA (log2FC -2.312) and protein (log2FC -1.658) and replicates in TCGA-KIRC (log2FC -2.815). Higher expression is protective (Cox log HR -0.402, padj 0.0000014). This reflects loss of tubule identity, in contrast to CA9, which is up.

caveats: Cohort is 110 tumours with 75 matched RNA normals and 84 matched proteome normals. Bulk tumour-versus-normal differences are partly confounded by tissue composition, so purity-extrapolated values were used where available.
DepMap ccRCC dependency effects are near zero or non-selective for most top up-regulated genes, so target status rests on expression and tractability and not on functional dependency.
Only the top 15 rows of the target and biomarker profiles were reviewed in detail. The top-40 convergence output was too large to read in full.
Phospho values are gene-level and not adjusted for protein abundance. They were not quoted, and site-level phosphorylation and kinase activity were not analysed.
VHL, PBRM1, SETD2 and BAP1 driver status and 3p loss were not queried in this pass.
